beats.text: Now SAM, properly. Its **encoder** is a plain vision transformer, B size: twelve blocks, and seven hundred sixty-eight channels.
A sixteen pixel patch becomes one **token**. In our run, a two hundred fifty-six pixel image gives a sixteen by sixteen grid of tokens.
Most blocks look inside small **windows**. Blocks three, six, nine and twelve look at the **whole** image.
The paper taps six, nine and twelve. So it takes features from **global** blocks.
Normally SAM adds a **prompt** encoder and a mask decoder. SAMBA-UNet drops the prompts, and keeps only the **encoder**.
Inside every block the paper adds **two** things: low-rank updates on the query and the value, and two small bottleneck adapters.
The rest stays **frozen**: about ninety million weights. The trainable extras are two and a half million, in our implementation.
